title: Review uncertainty before retaining a claim
brief: Make two bounded review decisions without mixing aircraft: the trainer pitch screen and the separate engine-out yaw screen. Explain why nominal success is not enough.
supplied: Which control claims survive conservative uncertainty bounds in the trainer pitch case and the separate twin-engine yaw case?
Trainer chapter rounded screen: available=4000±300 N m; required=1350±200 N m. Separate yaw aircraft: nominal available=8600 N m and required=7440 N m; test 10% less capacity and 5% more demand.
Nominal and conservative margins with a condition-specific decision for each aircraft.
Use stated interval bounds, not a probability of safety. The chapter rounds trainer capacity to 4.00 kN m for this uncertainty example.
Neither favorable static pitch arithmetic nor a nominal yaw pass establishes transient mission performance. Do not transfer evidence between the two aircraft.
The trainer interval margin remains positive; the separate yaw case becomes slightly negative under both adverse changes.
Yaw nominal margin=1160; with only 10% capacity loss=300; with both adverse changes=-72 N m. Preserve the failure rather than rounding it away.
Display separate aircraft and conditions; record requirement, model, evidence, decision, limitation and next evidence.
Sweep yaw capacity loss while applying the stated 5% demand increase; compare the resulting margin with zero.
